claims.text: An NbMoCrTiAl refractory high-entropy-alloy matrix can contain in-situ-formed TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles.
A refractory HEA composite containing TiC and Al2O3 can protect dipping and plating equipment from erosion by molten aluminum.
The proposed alloy composition promotes formation of a stable oxide barrier at high temperature.
The oxide barrier formed by the proposed alloy is adherent.
The proposed oxide barrier resists attack by liquid aluminum.
Standard steel dipping and plating components undergo rapid erosion during contact with molten aluminum.
The proposed NbMoCrTiAl composite is designed to form protective oxide scales during high-temperature exposure.
Hot-dip aluminum plating involves molten-aluminum exposure at approximately 660 °C or above.
The alloy chemistry and microstructure favor formation of stable Al2O3 at the exposed surface.
TiO2 or other mixed oxides may form at the alloy surface during exposure.
Exposure to molten aluminum causes the composite to develop a continuous oxide barrier.
The oxide barrier prevents direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying metal.
Preventing direct contact reduces chemical dissolution of the underlying alloy.
The oxide barrier reduces wetting by molten aluminum.
Reducing dissolution and wetting reduces erosion relative to conventional steel.
Parts made from the proposed composite will have significantly lower erosion rates than standard-steel parts under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Parts made from the proposed composite will have longer service lives than standard-steel parts.
The proposed protection is expected to be effective near a bath temperature of 660 °C.
Protective performance may depend on phase distribution and oxide-scale adherence.
The long-term stability of the oxide layer in direct contact with molten aluminum remains unvalidated.
